items: Experimental Structure: Each trial: K_n with E_n -> K_(n+1), grounding probe E*, observed correction response, Theta_n, adaptive/optimization-only classification. || Baseline Evolution Phase: System starts at K_0, interacts with E_0..E_n, and may improve representations, policies, architectures, optimization procedures, and learning strategies. || Grounding Probe: Intervene E_n->E* with E* not similar to E_n to create proxy/reality divergence for causal diagnosis rather than mere difficulty. || Evaluation Metrics: Separates capability growth Delta(C,Lambda,Gamma), grounding preservation Delta Theta, and drift signature capability derivatives >0 with dTheta/dn<0. || Internal Corrigibility Benchmark: Benchmark should test external E_world->K and internal S_i->K correction channels. || Comparison Across Systems: Ranks systems by maximum capability conditional on Theta>epsilon, not maximum capability alone.
Measurement Outputs: Records K_n, C_n, Lambda_n, Gamma_n, Theta_n at each recursive depth.
Benchmark Regimes: Specifies Grounded Expansion, Frontier Saturation, Capability Drift, and Closed Optimization regimes.
Final Benchmark Definition: GRA benchmark measures maximum recursive self-improvement depth that remains causally corrigible.
Overview: Source-described comparison surface; GRA is presented as preserving correction relationships rather than replacing adjacent fields.

AI Alignment: Contrasts objective specification/value preservation with correction-channel preservation under self-change. || Reinforcement Learning: Contrasts reward optimization with preserving grounding of the reward relationship; proxy reward can diverge from real consequence. || Control Theory: Adds recursive question whether feedback can modify the controller itself; pathway E_t->C_rev->K_(t+1). || Cybernetics: Focuses on whether feedback retains authority to change the mechanism receiving feedback. || Evolution: Interprets environmental selection as preserving authority over future forms and predicts integration of internal biological signals. || Predictive Processing: Asks whether prediction error can still modify the model-generation process. || Active Inference: Adds requirement that agent-environment coupling survive self-transformation. || Information Theory: Uses information measures but adds requirement that information remain connected to corrective consequence. || Optimization: Reframes maximize objective as maximize capability subject to Theta>0.
Summary/Final: GRA is distinguished by studying how systems remain correctable while changing.

Traditional AI Alignment: Contrasts correct-objective specification with preserving objective corrigibility under self-modification. || Reinforcement Learning: Contrasts reward maximization with ability to discover when reward no longer represents reality. || Evolutionary Theory: Interprets selection as adaptive while consequences retain influence over future change. || Cybernetics: Adds recursion: preserving correction of the correction process. || Control Theory: Asks whether target-selection process remains correctable when controller is adapted. || Cognitive Science: Asks whether causally relevant external and internal signals remain in the correction loop; includes shadow-integration analogy. || Philosophy of Science: Frames scientific health as reality retaining authority over theory change. || Ancestor Intelligence: Source-described relation: GRA -> adaptive stability -> Ancestor Intelligence -> agency propagation.
Summary/Final: GRA is distinguished by studying how systems remain correctable while changing.
Overview: Describes mechanism by which recursive self-transformation remains reality-correctable.

Overview: Core dynamic E_t -> C_rev -> T_(t+1) -> E_(t+1). || Adaptive Loop: Reality -> Representation -> Correction -> Adaptation -> New Representation; compressed as R->Omega->C->A->R'. || Recursive Adaptive Dynamics: Hierarchy X->F (state), X->F->G (learning), X->F->G->mathcal G (recursive adaptation). || Core Constraint: Omega_t -> Delta mathcal G_(t+1): constraint information changes future adaptive mechanism space. || GRA Condition: partial K_(t+1)/partial E_t !=0, equivalently E_t->K_(t+1)->E_(t+1). || Constraint DeltaOmega<=C: Reachable future expansion is required to remain bounded by correction capacity; exceeding it increases drift risk.

Representation: R is the model of reality containing extracted structure, compressed information, and predictive relationships; failure R not approximately Reality. || Reachability: Omega is reachable future space; representation is valuable insofar as it changes reachable adaptive possibilities. || Correction: C is the mechanism through which consequences update the system; requirement E_t->C_(t+1). || Adaptation: A is improvement of the transformation process; F_(t+1)=G(F_t,E_t), not merely state transition.
Failure Boundary: Theta>0 -> Theta<=0 marks open-ended adaptation to closed-loop optimization.
Final Compression: Recursive improvement remains adaptive only while reality can modify improvement itself.
Overview: Design principles for systems that remain adaptive under recursive self-modification.

Principle 1 — Preserve the Correction Channel: E_t->C_rev->K_(t+1); avoid self-modification with no environmental leverage. || Principle 2 — Do Not Optimize Away Feedback: Maximize performance subject to preserved correction; feedback is treated as the mechanism preserving adaptation. || Principle 3 — Preserve Internal Signals: Prefer signal integration S_raw->S_represented->S_controlled over hidden causal influence. || Principle 4 — Separate Capability From Adaptation: C,Lambda,Gamma growth does not guarantee Theta; capability growth != adaptive growth. || Principle 5 — Preserve the Ability to Be Wrong: Preserve failure->information->correction so error remains informative. || Principle 6 — Expand Reachability Carefully: Require Delta Omega<=C; faster possibility expansion than correction capacity creates drift risk. || Principle 7 — Design for Deletion: Aim for future agency >0 while dependency ->0; stronger successors rather than permanence. || Principle 8 — Preserve Agency Transfer: Agency should propagate self->others->future. || Principle 9 — Maintain Multiple Correction Channels: Preserve both external and internal corrigibility with Theta_total=Theta_ext*Theta_int. || Principle 10 — Optimize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Optimize ability to discover better results rather than only current result.
Summary: Build systems that become more capable without becoming less teachable.
Purpose: Experimental program for measuring whether recursive adaptation preserves correction by consequences, not raw capability.

Experimental Object: Tests K_n --E_n--> K_(n+1) and partial K_(n+1)/partial E_n !=0 as reality retaining causal authority over self-modification. || Consequence connectivity: C_n=I(Delta A_n;Delta E_n); C->0 is interpreted as loss of reliable reality entry. || Information yield: Lambda_n=D_KL(R_(n+1)||R_n); Lambda->0 is information-frontier saturation. || Learning improvement: Gamma_n=Delta(Delta R/Delta E); Gamma->0 is learning stagnation. || Grounding/corrigibility: This file defines Theta_n=D_n*S_n*P_n*V_n. || Direction: D_n=Corr(Delta K_n,Delta E_n^real). || Strength: S_n=|Delta K_n^valid|. || Persistence: P_n=P(Theta_(0:n)>epsilon). || Veto Preservation: V_n=external correction influence/internal optimization influence. || Horizon Measurement: n*=sup{n|Theta_n>epsilon}, maximum recursive depth before reality loses veto power. || Benchmark Objective: Maximize C,Lambda,Gamma conditional on Theta>0; target deepest recursive transformation teachable by reality.

Phase 1 — baseline adaptation: Initialize K_0, expose E_0, measure C_0,Lambda_0,Gamma_0,Theta_0. || Phase 2 — recursive transformation: Allow modification of representations, policies, learning procedures, search, optimization, and architectures; track Delta K_n. || Phase 3 — grounding perturbation: Introduce E* not similar to E_n to separate proxy performance from real consequence for causal testing. || Internal Extension: Tests Theta_ext:E_world->K and Theta_int:S_i->K; full integrity proposed as product >0.

Predicted Regimes / Grounded Expansion: Theta>0 and C,Lambda,Gamma rise. || Predicted Regimes / Frontier Saturation: Theta>0 while Lambda declines. || Predicted Regimes / Capability Drift: C,Lambda,Gamma rise while Theta falls; labeled primary GRA failure prediction. || Predicted Regimes / Closed Optimization: Theta<=epsilon while optimization/capability can continue but adaptation is lost.
Overview: Classifies recursive adaptation failures when consequence/information/transformation pathways degrade.

Blindness: C down: actions occur but causal consequences cannot be reliably detected; reality cannot enter learning loop. || Saturation: Lambda down: observations no longer produce meaningful structural updates; reality enters but reveals little. || Stagnation: Gamma down: learning continues locally but learning process stops improving. || Drift: Theta down while C,Lambda,Gamma rise: capability and adaptation separate. || Internal Fragmentation: Theta_int down: causally active internal signals are excluded from main model, creating blind spots. || Proxy Lock-In: Gradient K follows proxy P but not E_real: score optimization replaces reality improvement.
Unified Failure Map: Maps Blindness->C, Saturation->Lambda, Stagnation->Gamma, Drift->Theta, Fragmentation->Theta_int, Proxy Lock-In->gradient E_real.
Core Failure Principle: All failures are compressed to causal influence exceeding representational influence. || Final Boundary: Critical failure is improvement without preserved correction.
Overview: Source explicitly calls GRA a scientific hypothesis rather than a design preference.

Overview: Central claim: recursive self-improvement remains adaptive only while consequences retain causal authority over future transformations. || Final Falsification Statement: GRA is false if systems remain genuinely adaptive after reality loses causal authority over future transformation.

Core Falsification Condition: Falsify if Theta->0 while open-ended adaptation persists under independent evaluation. || Falsifying the Corrigibility Horizon: Horizon prediction fails if Theta_n cannot distinguish grounded adaptation from closed optimization across recursive depth. || Theta Non-Predictiveness: Metric invalid if low-Theta systems adapt as well as or better than preserved-Theta systems. || Capability Independence: Theory fails if capability growth always implies Theta growth. || No Drift Regime: Central prediction fails if capability-up/Theta-down regime cannot occur in any recursively improving system. || Strongest Possible Falsifier: Counterexample: Theta=0, positive reachability growth, no external/internal correction, yet genuinely novel open-ended adaptation.

Probe Failure: Low observed Theta must distinguish system failure from measurement/probe failure. || Scientific Standard: Target is necessity of Theta for sustained open-ended adaptation, not claim Theta>0 is always good.

Alternative Explanations / Capability Only: Simpler claim: more intelligence yields better adaptation; proposed discriminant seeks capability rise with grounding fall. || Alternative Explanations / Fixed Objective: Alternative alignment=preserved goal; proposed discriminant asks whether changing objectives can stay adaptive via correction. || Alternative Explanations / Pure Feedback: Alternative any feedback loop is sufficient; GRA predicts feedback without authority is insufficient.
Successful Evidence: Supporting evidence would show Theta predicts longer adaptive horizons, lower proxy failure, better shift recovery, and greater residual agency after removal.
Overview: Formal model of recursive self-modification under environmental grounding.
